Preprint — arXiv, 4-page short paper; no venue stated
Independent researcher, China (xiaojinpro.com e-mail); the author develops the projects used (jarvis, jarvis-forge, MissionD)

Proposes an approach; secondary: Compares — intent.lisp, an S-expression architecture descriptor for coding agents; controlled experiments compare context conditions (Blind vs S-expression, JSON, Markdown; Blind vs AutoGen vs Curated descriptors), plus a writer-side generation/error-resilience experiment and an observational field study

intent.lisp (proposed), with the forge survey tool; no version. Compared formats: same descriptor in S-expression, JSON, YAML (writer side only) and Markdown; AutoGen (auto-generated, ~170 lines) vs Curated (hand-refined, 698 lines) descriptors

One architecture descriptor file (intent.lisp) per project: nested S-expression tree of pillars (responsibility domains), components (modules) and symbols (function signatures, types, constants), plus design constraints, invariants, roles and data flows

Descriptor lifecycle: (1) Generation: survey tool scans the AST and an LLM drafts the descriptor (developer describes intent in natural language, LLM translates it to S-expressions); (2) Consumption: agents use it as navigation entry point (injected into the system prompt in the experiments; read via tool calls in the field study); (3) Co-evolution: updated with code changes and version-controlled
Optional hand refinement of the descriptor (Curated condition); AutoGen used with zero human editing. No other review points stated
Single artefact (architecture descriptor used as context) for code localization; code modification not exercised
Not classifiable; descriptor co-evolves with code and is version-controlled (closest to spec-anchored, draft). Author relates it to 'specification-driven development' (spec-kit, Kiro, Self-Spec)
Existing code bases: code localization tasks (no code modification)

Exp. 1 (24 tasks, jarvis); agent/harness not stated + Claude Sonnet 4.6, temp 0, max 20 steps; criterion: correct localization, steps. Quality and cost verdicts for every entry: no criterion stated by the authors. (a) Blind + n.s. + Sonnet 4.6 (baseline): acc 54% (13/24), 5.2 steps. (b) S-expression context: 58%, 3.4 steps, d=0.92 vs blind (p=0.009). (c) JSON context: 58%, 3.4 steps, d=1.02. (d) Markdown context: 63%, 2.9 steps, d=1.43 (p=0.005). Comprehension study (20 questions, model not stated): 95% accuracy for S-expr, JSON, YAML and Markdown. Exp. E (15 tasks, jarvis-forge; agent and model not stated for this experiment): (e) Blind (baseline): 80%, 5.6 steps, censored mean 8.5. (f) AutoGen descriptor: 100%, 3.9 steps, censored 3.9 (p=0.002, d=1.04). (g) Curated descriptor: 87%, 2.9 steps, censored 5.2 (p=0.003). Writer side (model not stated, temp 0): parse validity JSON 100%, S-expr 95.8%, YAML 91.7%; overall error detection S-expr 50%, JSON 62%, YAML 21%, MD 0%; silent corruption 50/21/50/100%. Field study (Claude Code, model not stated): explore/edit IQR 2.24 -> 1.08 after descriptors introduced (observational, no control)

Exp. 1: 24 code localization tasks on one Rust project; 4 conditions (Blind, S-expr, JSON, Markdown context injected into the system prompt); baseline Blind; held constant: model (Claude Sonnet 4.6), temperature 0, max 20 steps, tasks; acceptance tests: none described; repetitions: not stated (apparently 1 run per task). Exp. E: 15 tasks, 3 conditions (Blind, AutoGen, Curated). Writer side: 3 repetitions. Field study: before/after introduction of descriptors in two projects (no control). Human intervention: not stated. Tasks not randomly selected

Context vs blind: 33-44% fewer steps (Wilcoxon p<0.015, d 0.92-1.43); accuracy +4 to +9 points (significance not reported). Formats: no significant difference (all pairwise p>0.07; only 3-6 effective paired differences). AutoGen vs blind: 100% vs 80% (p=0.002); Curated vs blind p=0.003; AutoGen vs Curated not significant (p=0.515). Field study: 52% lower explore/edit IQR; sessions reading intent.lisp vs not: 1.65 vs 1.65

Distinguished context vs no context on steps; did not distinguish formats (underpowered, stated by the author). Repeatability: temperature 0, single model; effect model-sensitive (earlier weaker model d=1.70). Limitations stated: low statistical power, only localization tasks, non-randomized task selection, small test project (22K lines), context delivery mismatch between experiment and field study; five tasks failed in all conditions due to descriptor staleness

Effect model-sensitive and may shrink on small projects; needs evaluation on larger code bases (100K+ lines); multi-file modification and architectural decisions untested; multi-agent subtree partitioning future work; detailed descriptors may matter for governance tasks not tested; format comparison underpowered
